prompt:
Original Taiwanese game art for "Tainan Gazetteer" (府城夜巡地圖), set in Tainan around 1930.
Style: handmade layered paper sculpture (紙雕 / kirie), the same for buildings, trees, plants,
fences, ground tiles, icons and props. Every shape is a piece of cut paper: visible paper fibres,
slightly soft hand-cut edges, pieces overlapping in shallow layers with small soft contact shadows
where one sheet sits on another. Colour is printed on the paper: clearly visible risograph /
stencil print grain and uneven ink density across every flat area, never a clean digital fill.
Weathering is welcome: irregular faded patches, not neat squares.
Details are built from few, large cut pieces (roof tiles, bricks, window frames, leaves, petals,
stones, planks), not painted lines and not crowded tiny patterns. Plants are natural and
asymmetric.
Colour: follow the real object, then mute it: pale, slightly greyed, warm. Typical tones: warm
cream, pale brick red, coral, sage and grey-green, mustard, indigo, wood brown, stone grey.
No saturated red-against-green contrast.
Buildings: strictly frontal elevation, no perspective, three or four flat paper layers.
Do NOT make: a 3D render or clay/plastic model, smooth bevelled relief, realistic or painterly
illustration, photo textures, thick foam layers, glow, glossy highlights, black outline strokes,
smooth gradients, depth of field.
Output: generated natively on a fully TRANSPARENT background (real alpha including enclosed
holes, no backdrop, no glow, no chroma-key colour, no coloured fringe), every object complete
and separated by clear transparent gutters, no ground, no base, no cast shadow outside the
object, no text, no captions, no logos.

Create treesA.png, a single landscape sprite sheet with exactly six complete trees on a regular three-column by two-row grid. Row-major order is fixed. Keep each silhouette entirely inside its equal-size cell with generous transparent straight gutters at both column boundaries and the row boundary. Fit each species in its cell while preserving its own width-to-height ratio, with all tips and roots visible. No marks or grid lines.

Image 1 is the primary style reference: use only its lower-left cherry and lower-middle maple as the approved examples of warm fibrous paper wood, angular bends with changing widths, broad irregular overlapping paper canopy pieces and print grain. Image 2 demonstrates the idea of angular folded-paper branch segments and large rounded leaf masses. Invent species-specific silhouettes and branch geometries instead of tracing that example. Images 3 and 4 are the current banyan and rainTree sprites; preserve their species silhouettes and proportions while recutting canopy and trunk as specified. Image 5 is a Tainan Confucius Temple area tree photo for real-world branching proportions. Follow the detailed species notes below for the remaining four trees.

Emphasize clearly angular elbows in silhouette on the spreading trees: use short straight sections joined at visible changes of direction, taper in distinct stages, and fork obliquely. Construct these as overlapping flat fibrous paper cutouts, with shallow contact shadows within the silhouette only. Avoid smooth tubular S-curves, realistic bark, dense small leaf patterns, symmetrical mirrored branch shapes and evenly spaced tiers. Canopy sheets have broad rounded contours with a few irregular lobes, visible overlaps, muted warm greyed hues, and softly mottled ink.

Top left, banyan: massive rooted trunk, stout angular boughs folding outward at different heights to both sides, a few thin angular hanging aerial roots, and three or four broad rounded dark muted green canopy masses.
Top center, rainTree: very broad shallow umbrella silhouette, long lateral boughs with conspicuous bends and open gaps below the canopy, two or three broad rounded pale yellow-green canopy masses, unequal reach on each side.
Top right, plumeria: compact silhouette with short thick grey trunk repeatedly forking at angles, a few branch-end clusters of large elongated leaves and white five-petalled flowers with yellow centers.
Bottom left, flameTree: broad spreading silhouette with clearly angular horizontal boughs, a few large green canopy sheets accented with restrained orange-red flower clusters.
Bottom center, norfolkPine: tall, slender, nearly straight slightly leaning trunk, plenty of bare lower trunk, irregularly spaced sparse tiers of horizontally folded boughs with slightly drooping angular tips, unequal lengths and occasional missing branches. Natural park-tree habit, not a dense symmetrical Christmas-tree cone.
Bottom right, royalPalm: upright straight pale grey trunk made of distinctly stacked paper segments, olive-grey green crownshaft and a few large folded pinnate fronds with unequal fans and visible paper edges.
Generate directly with transparent alpha, including open gaps between branches. No background tint, exterior shadow, halo, colored fringe, or extra objects.

Critical production layout: Use a wide 3:2 canvas whose six identical crop cells are bounded at exactly 1/3 and 2/3 of the width and halfway down the height. Center the respective trees at x=16.7%, 50%, 83.3%, and y=25%, 75%. Each tree must fit within the central 84% of its own cell in both dimensions, scaling down wide trees when necessary and preserving their true proportions. At the exact halfway and third lines, all pixels must be fully clear. Color must exist only inside the cut-paper silhouettes. Treat the page as six physically separate die-cut paper stickers with pure transparent empty space, no backdrop, no diffuse aura.

Prioritize generous gutters over sprite size. Make the six trees distinctly smaller relative to the page, occupying at most 70% of each cell width and 78% of each cell height. Aim for wide consistently blank transparent corridors between all three columns and between both rows, and a generous transparent margin all around. Especially scale down all of the broad-canopied trees until these corridors are conspicuous.
notes: 原生透明背景由內建 image_gen 生成，保留原始 PNG 與 alpha。輸入依序為核可圖集、折紙樹幹概念圖、現行榕樹、現行雨豆樹、孔廟實景照。另比對其餘四棵現行圖。實景參考：榕樹與雨豆樹 https://serv-oga.ncku.edu.tw/p/406-1057-256133%2Cr1325.php?Lang=zh-tw 、https://oldtree.life/oldtree/4176 ；雞蛋花 https://www.nparks.gov.sg/FloraFaunaWeb/Flora/3/0/3074 ；鳳凰木 https://www.nparks.gov.sg/florafaunaweb/flora/2/8/2838 ；南洋杉 https://www.tcavs.tc.edu.tw/forestry/7-2.asp?proid=20180828142651 ；大王椰子 https://www.nparks.gov.sg/florafaunaweb/flora/2/6/2682 。
